problem: Internal architecture of 'pool_membership_manager' (type: Subservice — Internal control-plane subservice running as part of chain_router; holds no canonical state outside chain_router's stores; mutations are local but coordinate over region_coordinator for cross-region truths.). Node: Owns admit/evict decisions for chain pool replicas across all (chain, fork_id) sub-pools: replicas are admitted into a sub-pool, transitioned through healthy/draining/evicted/quarantined lifecycle states, and the per-(chain, fork_id) sub-pool membership is the canonical source for which replicas serve traffic in this region. Lifecycle transitions in pool_registry are gated on the replica's current drain_state_log entry: admit requires drain-completed-or-aborted, evict requires drain-completed; concurrent proposals are CAS-ordered through pool_registry per shard so admit-during-drain or evict-after-readmit cannot both commit. Re-admission of a draining replica requires an explicit drain-abort transition before admit can commit; auto-admit cannot transition a replica with drain_state_log = drain-in-progress without first proposing drain-abort, surfacing an alert with attribution. On dispatch the manager re-validates the replica's currently-recorded fork_id against the request's (chain, fork_id) tag at the moment of dispatch (not just at routing-table read time); a mismatch returns a retryable-on-other-replica signal. Refuses any quarantine eviction whose commit would push the (chain, fork_id) sub-pool's healthy-replica count below the documented safe-membership floor; refusal surfaces an alert with the (chain, fork_id) at risk. Computes the effective-capacity denominator (count of replicas currently admitted AND not draining AND not in deferred-quarantine AND not tip-stale) from per-(chain, fork_id) pool_registry shard summaries on every relevant transition and propagates it to sub_pool_fork_partitioner. Exposes a per-(chain, fork_id) target-capacity surface; when traffic share exceeds target by a documented margin, proposes membership rebalances gated on safe-membership floor for both source and destination sub-pools, committed via the same CAS path. Records per-replica replica-class (tip-serving / historical-archive / both) in pool_registry; refuses to admit a tip-class request to an archive-only replica and vice versa. COST-CLASS DISPATCH: refuses any dispatch lacking a cost-class hint when the request type requires one (long-RPC archive paths) and surfaces an alert if a cost-class-less retry arrives at dispatch (so a retry that lost its hint cannot be silently mis-routed). DRAIN-FENCE BROADCAST CONSUMER: pool_membership_manager (with drain_coordinator) consumes lifecycle_gate-originated drain-fence broadcasts for tenant T as self-contained credential bundles, verifies the signature against the broadcast's NAMED roster_version (via on-demand named-roster fetch from region_coordinator when V_named is strictly newer than the local cache, bounded by an HLC budget tighter than the per-tenant ack window; on fetch failure rejects with a typed 'named-roster-unfetchable' attestation to compliance_audit; bulk waves coalesce named-roster fetches into one). On verified broadcast, flushes in-flight audit writes for tenant T to compliance_audit then acks drain to tenant_store within the HLC-bounded ack window. PRIORITY LANE: drain-fence flush takes priority on the per-(chain, fork_id) pool_registry shard CAS line (tagged drain-fence-priority and pre-empts deferred-quarantine commits); deferred-quarantines wait until drain-fence ACK-EMITTED; surfaces an alert when quarantine deferral grows under drain-fence pressure. DRAIN-FENCE VS FORK-TRANSITION FENCE: refuses to commit a drain-ack while a fork-transition handshake is mid-flight on any (chain, fork_id) shard whose audit writes for tenant T are in flight; ack-window HLC budget extends across handshake completion or the broadcast is rejected with a typed 'drain-fence-blocked-by-fork-transition' attestation; flush enumerates audit writes by tenant_id across both pre- and post-transition sub-pool views. PHASE-MARKERS: maintains a durable per-(offboarding_id, component_id) apply-state record with typed phase-markers (RECEIVED, FLUSH-IN-PROGRESS, FLUSH-COMPLETE, ACK-EMITTED, ATTESTATION-WRITTEN, TERMINAL-ACK, TERMINAL-PRESERVATION-BLOCKED); on restart resumes from the last durable phase and never re-runs a non-idempotent phase; never retracts a drain-ack. TERMINAL-CLASS ATTESTATION: each terminal class writes exactly one typed attestation to compliance_audit under the (offboarding_id, component_id, attempt_id) idempotency key; canonical writer election by drain_state_log CAS shared with drain_coordinator. OPERATOR-OVERRIDE: operator-override admission (used during emergency rollover) requires M-of-N operator quorum signatures on the admit proposal — signing operators are recorded with the admit commit and visible in audit. ROSTER VERIFICATION: caches operator-credential roster locally with documented HLC-bounded freshness window; falls to deny-by-default for further override admissions when cached roster is older than the freshness window or no roster has ever been received; deny is sticky until a strictly-newer roster_version ack-readies. Override-commit path verifies the proposal against region_coordinator's currently-active roster_version (named-roster lookup, not local cache) at commit time, including evaluation of any retroactive-as-of-HLC compromise-revocation predating the proposal's submission HLC; commit fails closed if any signing credential is retroactively revoked; pre-commit roster_version is re-checked atomically with the pool_registry CAS commit so the activation race cannot slip between roster check and registry commit. Rejects proposals whose signing roster_version predates the currently-effective roster_version. Enforces a documented max-overrides-per-window rate limit on operator-override admissions that bypass safe-membership floor. Reads pool_registry through the per-(chain, fork_id) shard plus shard-level summaries for cross-shard consumers.. Connections: sub_pool_fork_partitioner --calls-> pool_membership_manager; pool_membership_manager --calls-> response_canonicalizer; drain_coordinator --calls-> pool_membership_manager; pool_membership_manager --writes_to-> pool_registry; pool_membership_manager --reads_from-> pool_registry; pool_membership_manager --reads_from-> quarantine_set. Parent requirements: IR-fork-sub-pool-partition: Each chain pool is partitioned by (chain_id, fork_id) so per-fork sub-pools serve fork-specific traffic; routing of an incoming RPC tagged with (chain, fork) goes only to the matching sub-pool, and replicas across forks are sub-pool members rather than divergent peers.; IR-pool-drain-protocol: A replica entering 'draining' state stops receiving new requests, finishes in-flight RPCs (or returns them with a retryable-on-other-replica hint), and only after gateway has re-bound dependent subscriptions does the replica unsubscribe from fanout's head streams; eviction commits only after gateway-rebind acknowledgement.; IR-schema-skew-quarantine: When a replica's canonicalized response shape diverges from the (chain, method, schema_version) pool consensus shape, the replica is quarantined from the active sub-pool and the divergence evidence is surfaced to operators.; IR-offboarding-idempotency: Cancellation of in-flight long-RPCs for offboarded tenants dedupes inbound offboarding signals from region_coordinator by idempotency key (offboarding_id, component_id, attempt_id), meets a documented attestation SLO, and surfaces preservation-blocked terminal states (e.g. when an in-flight long-RPC overlaps a preservation hold) so region_coordinator can record best-effort attestations rather than waiting indefinitely.; SR-replica-fork-revalidate: On dispatch to a replica, pool_membership_manager re-validates the replica's currently-recorded fork_id in pool_registry against the request's (chain, fork_id) tag at the moment of dispatch (not just at routing-table read time); a mismatch returns a retryable-on-other-replica signal rather than answering with cross-fork data, so a fork transition cannot answer an old-fork request with new-fork data.; SR-drain-state-cas-gate: pool_registry lifecycle transitions for a replica are gated on the replica's current drain_state_log entry: a transition to admitted requires drain-completed-or-aborted, a transition to evicted requires drain-completed; concurrent proposals are CAS-ordered through pool_registry so admit-during-drain or evict-after-readmit cannot both commit.; SR-drain-abort-explicit: Re-admission of a draining replica requires an explicit drain-abort transition in drain_state_log before the admit can commit; pool_membership_manager cannot auto-admit a replica whose drain_state_log entry is drain-in-progress without first proposing drain-abort, which surfaces an alert and records the operator/system attribution.; SR-quarantine-mass-evict-cap: schema_skew_quarantine enforces a per-(chain, fork_id) max-concurrent-quarantine-commits cap within a documented window; quarantine commits beyond the cap are deferred and surfaced as an alert listing the deferred replicas. The cap is at most a documented fraction of sub-pool membership so quarantine cannot push a sub-pool below the safe-membership floor in a single window.; SR-quarantine-floor-gate: Before a quarantine eviction commits in pool_registry via pool_membership_manager, the manager refuses the transition if it would push the (chain, fork_id) sub-pool's healthy-replica count below the documented safe-membership floor; refusal surfaces an alert with the (chain, fork_id) at risk and the candidate replica.; SR-sub-pool-capacity-rebalance: pool_membership_manager exposes a documented per-(chain, fork_id) sub-pool target-capacity surface; when traffic share for a sub-pool exceeds its target by a documented margin, the manager proposes membership rebalances (admit additional replicas of that fork, drain over-provisioned rare-fork replicas) gated on the safe-membership floor for both the source and destination sub-pools. Rebalance proposals are committed via the same pool_registry CAS path as drain/admit and are visible in the audit.; SR-effective-capacity-denominator: pool_membership_manager's request-admission and per-replica load computations use the effective-capacity denominator (count of replicas currently admitted AND not draining AND not in deferred-quarantine AND not tip-stale) rather than total pool_registry membership; the denominator is recomputed on every relevant pool_registry transition and propagated to sub_pool_fork_partitioner's routing decisions so per-replica fan-out reflects the actually-serving subset.; SR-pool-admit-override-mofn: pool_membership_manager's operator-override admission path (used to admit replacement replicas faster than blue/green allows during emergency rollover) requires M-of-N operator quorum signatures (configurable threshold) carried with the admit proposal rather than a single operator credential; signing operators are recorded with the admit commit and visible in subsequent membership audit. The credential model and key custody are parent scope's responsibility (bubbled).; SR-pool-admit-override-rate-limit: pool_membership_manager enforces a documented max-overrides-per-window rate limit on operator-override admissions that bypass the safe-membership-floor; approaching the limit surfaces an alert; exceeding it rejects further override admits with a documented error code visible to the operator path.; SR-pool-registry-shard-by-fork: pool_registry is sharded by (chain, fork_id): each sub-pool's lifecycle entries live in their own shard with independent CAS lines so high-rate transitions on one sub-pool do not contend with reads or writes on others. Cross-shard reads (e.g. effective-capacity denominator) consume shard-level summaries rather than scanning the global registry.; SR-replica-class-tip-vs-archive: pool_registry records each replica's replica-class (tip-serving / historical-archive / both) per (chain, fork_id, replica_id); sub_pool_fork_partitioner uses the cost-class hint of the inbound RPC (short-RPC tip-sensitive vs long-RPC archive) to route only to a replica whose class includes the request's class. pool_membership_manager refuses to admit a tip-class request to an archive-only replica and vice versa, so heavy archive queries cannot saturate tip-serving capacity.; IIR-drain-fence-broadcast-consume: chain_router consumes the lifecycle_gate-originated drain-fence broadcast for tenant T: drain_coordinator and pool_membership_manager flush in-flight audit writes for T to compliance_audit and ack drain to tenant_store within the HLC-bounded ack window; the drain-fence broadcast is verified as a self-contained credential bundle (broadcast names roster_version; verification is against the named roster_version, not the local cache).; IIR-broadcast-named-roster-verify: Every signed broadcast consumed by chain_router subsystems (offboarding signal, drain-fence broadcast, lifecycle-gate-scheduled drain window, roster updates) is treated as a self-contained credential bundle: chain_router verifies the signature against the broadcast's NAMED roster_version, not the locally cached roster_version, and rejects broadcasts whose named roster_version is unknown or has been retroactively revoked. Local roster cache acts only as the freshness witness, not as the authority.; IIR-roster-freshness-window: chain_router caches the operator-credential roster locally with a documented HLC-bounded freshness window; pool_membership_manager and drain_coordinator fall to deny-by-default for further override admissions when the cached roster is older than the freshness window or when no roster has ever been received; deny is sticky for that override path until a strictly-newer roster_version ack-readies.; IIR-roster-version-rejection: pool_membership_manager and drain_coordinator reject any operator-override proposal whose signing roster_version predates chain_router's currently-effective roster_version, and refuse to commit overrides after a compromise-revocation invalidates any in-flight signature (including retroactive compromise-revocations whose retroactive-as-of-HLC predates the proposal's submission); cancel-and-rollback for in-flight proposals is performed atomically at activation by roster_version.; IIR-fork-transition-handshake-fanout: When fork_detection_alerter produces a sub-pool repartition for (chain, fork_id), chain_router emits a structured fork-transition handshake to fanout that names the divergence point (chain_id, prior fork_id, new fork_id, divergence height/HLC). The handshake protocol is initiated by sub_pool_fork_partitioner only after pool_membership_manager has committed the new sub-pool's membership in pool_registry and the routing-table fence has admitted the new fork; chain_router does not begin dispatching forward-progress requests on the new fork to fanout until fanout has acked the handshake.; IIR-offboarding-phase-markers: pool_membership_manager and drain_coordinator maintain a durable per-(offboarding_id, component_id) apply-state record with typed phase-markers (RECEIVED, FLUSH-IN-PROGRESS, FLUSH-COMPLETE, ACK-EMITTED, ATTESTATION-WRITTEN, TERMINAL); on restart resumes from the last durable phase and never re-runs a non-idempotent phase; never retracts a drain-ack once emitted; flush-in-progress includes flushing in-flight audit writes for the tenant to compliance_audit before ack-emit.; SR2-drain-fence-priority-lane: Drain-fence flush is admitted on a separate priority lane than quarantine commits on the per-(chain, fork_id) pool_registry shard CAS line: drain-fence transitions are tagged drain-fence-priority and pre-empt deferred-quarantine commits; deferred-quarantines wait until drain-fence ACK-EMITTED. pool_membership_manager surfaces an alert when quarantine deferral grows under drain-fence pressure.; SR2-named-roster-on-demand-fetch: chain_router exposes an on-demand named-roster fetch path: when a broadcast names V_named that is strictly newer than the local cache, chain_router synchronously requests V_named from region_coordinator over the cert-bearing inter-region surface before verifying the broadcast; the fetch is bounded by a documented HLC budget tighter than the per-tenant ack window; on fetch failure within budget, chain_router rejects the broadcast and emits a typed 'named-roster-unfetchable' attestation to compliance_audit with the offboarding_id.; SR2-terminal-class-attestation-distinct: Phase-marker taxonomy distinguishes TERMINAL-ACK from TERMINAL-PRESERVATION-BLOCKED; each terminal class writes exactly one typed attestation to compliance_audit with the (offboarding_id, component_id, attempt_id) idempotency key. drain_coordinator and pool_membership_manager share the same drain_state_log entry; the attestation writer is whichever subsystem reaches TERMINAL first under the idempotency key (canonical writer election by drain_state_log CAS).; SR2-cost-class-hint-retry-preserve: sub_pool_fork_partitioner attaches the original cost-class hint to the retryable-on-other-replica response signal so retry paths preserve it; pool_membership_manager refuses any dispatch lacking a cost-class hint when the request type requires one (long-RPC archive paths) and surfaces an alert if a cost-class-less retry arrives at dispatch.; SR2-override-commit-named-roster: pool_membership_manager's override-commit path verifies the proposal against region_coordinator's currently-active roster_version (named-roster lookup, not local cache) at commit time, including evaluation of any retroactive-as-of-HLC compromise-revocation that predates the proposal's submission HLC; commit fails closed if any signing credential is retroactively revoked. Pre-commit roster_version is re-checked atomically with the pool_registry CAS commit so the activation race cannot slip between roster check and registry commit.; SR2-drain-fence-vs-fork-transition-fence: Drain-fence flush is fenced against fork-transition handshake state: pool_membership_manager refuses to commit a drain-ack while a fork-transition handshake is mid-flight on any (chain, fork_id) shard whose audit writes for tenant T are in flight; the drain-fence ack window's HLC budget extends across handshake completion or the broadcast is rejected with a typed 'drain-fence-blocked-by-fork-transition' attestation to compliance_audit. Flush enumerates audit writes by tenant_id across both pre- and post-transition sub-pool views.; SR2-bulk-roster-fetch-coalesce: Bulk-offboarding wave triggers a single named-roster fetch for the shared roster_version: pool_membership_manager and drain_coordinator coalesce on the named-roster lookup so the wave does not trigger N fetch operations; on fetch failure, all broadcasts in the wave are rejected with a single typed 'named-roster-fetch-failed-bulk' attestation including the wave-id, allowing lifecycle_gate to retry the wave with bounded backoff before STRICT finalization.

versions.note: v0 — Naive: 12 internal nodes (5 Engine + 1 CommitGate + 3 EvidenceStore + 2 BroadcastConsumer + 1 DispatchGuard) wiring admit/evict + override + quarantine + sub-pool composition + effective-capacity through a per-(chain, fork_id) shard CAS commit_sequencer with drain-fence-priority lane, drain-fence broadcast consumer with named-roster fetch, roster broadcast consumer, and dispatch validator (cost-class + replica-class + fork_id revalidate). 19 initial reqs all satisfied; CRITICAL K̄=1.75 P̄=0.71 modularity=0.62; hotspots commit_sequencer K=6 and replica_health_register K=6.

v1 — Direction 21 Session 1: 5 stressors all BREAKING, 16 derived reqs (15 satisfied locally + 1 partially satisfied with parent-scope bubble bubble-pool_membership_manager-1 for bulk_admit budget contract). override_admission_engine gained: CAS witness (named-roster_version + retroactive-as-of-HLC frontier per signing credential) carried with proposal, atomic re-check by commit_sequencer with sequenced revocation log read under same shard lock, OVERRIDE-PROPOSED journal marker with witness fingerprint, separate emergency vs bulk_admit counters. roster_broadcast_consumer gained: sequenced revocation log publication (committed-versus-not). roster_cache redefined: explicitly purely freshness-witness, never authoritative. commit_sequencer gained: admission-class lane discriminator with drain-fence-priority pre-empt + round-robin fairness across non-priority lanes, fork_transition_state field (stable / reshape-committed-handshake-pending / handshake-acked) under shard CAS, atomic single-multi-row reshape commit, shard summary computed in CAS critical section stamped with commit_hlc_watermark. replica_health_register gained: lock-free reader path keyed by commit_hlc_watermark with stale-bound fallback, wave_id-keyed running counts (admitted-in-wave, evicted-in-wave). admit_evict_engine gained: shard-locked floor check, projected-post-wave-state floor check for bulk-wave admits, dual-view audit-write enumeration during fork-transition mid-reshape. quarantine_eviction_engine gained: shard-locked floor check, deferral-aged alert keyed by deferral_started_hlc replay-safe across crashes. dispatch_validator gained: out-of-band refusal alert path to refusal_alert_buffer, lock-free summary read with stale-watermark bounce, fork_transition_state read for forward-progress gating, tenant-keyed per-window refusal counters. New node refusal_alert_buffer (EvidenceStore) with writes_to_buffer edge (DispatchGuard -> EvidenceStore). NKP K̄=1.69 P̄=0.72 modularity=0.64, CRITICAL preserved; hotspots commit_sequencer K=6 and replica_health_register K=6 unchanged from v0.

stressors.description: A previously-trusted operator credential is retroactively compromised (retroactive-as-of-HLC predates submission HLC of an in-flight override admission proposal). Mid-admit: the proposal has passed M-of-N at submission; before commit, the compromise-revocation broadcast lands and is processed by roster_broadcast_consumer; meanwhile the override_admission_engine is in the middle of its commit-time named-roster lookup and the commit_sequencer's atomic re-check primitive must catch the activation race so the proposal cannot slip through. Question: does the activation race hold under concurrent override commit + retroactive-compromise propagation, given that roster_cache may be lagging, the named-roster fetch is in flight, AND another override proposal carrying a still-valid signature is racing on the same shard CAS line?
stressors.attractor: Either (a) override commits despite retroactive compromise because the engine's commit-time named-roster lookup races a concurrent compromise-revocation propagation and uses the still-stale fetch result, or (b) every override commit serializes behind compromise-revocation propagation across all shards, starving legitimate emergency rollovers, or (c) the engine and consumer disagree on the retroactive-as-of-HLC ordering and double-write conflicting attestations to the journal.
stressors.solution: v0 leaves the activation race underspecified at the boundary between override_admission_engine's commit-time named-roster lookup result and the commit_sequencer's atomic re-check. Solution: (1) override commits must carry the named-roster lookup's roster_version + retroactive-as-of-HLC frontier as a CAS witness alongside the proposal; commit_sequencer's atomic re-check refuses commit unless the witness's roster_version EQUALS the currently-effective roster_version AND the witness's retroactive-as-of-HLC frontier is no older than the latest compromise-revocation observed for any signing credential at re-check time. (2) roster_broadcast_consumer publishes compromise-revocations through a sequenced revocation log that commit_sequencer reads under the same CAS lock — propagation is committed-versus-not, not eventually-visible. (3) phase_marker_journal records OVERRIDE-PROPOSED with the witness fingerprint at submission so a restart cannot replay a stale-witnessed override commit. (4) roster_cache is purely a freshness-witness; it cannot be the source of the witness fingerprint.

stressors.description: A replica health-flaps (rapid healthy/unhealthy oscillation due to upstream chain-peer instability) during a lifecycle_gate-gated rotation window where parent-scope schema_skew_quarantine is consulting region_coordinator's rotation tag for suppression. The replica_health_register entries for that replica churn at high rate (each flap is a commit through commit_sequencer) and the effective_capacity_calculator recomputes the denominator on every transition; meanwhile drain_coordinator (outside this scope) attempts to schedule a drain inside the rotation window. Question: do replica_health_register's hlc_stamp-tagged entries stay coherent under flap rate, AND does the admit_evict_engine's safe-membership-floor read serialize correctly with the evicting drain race AND with the schema-skew quarantine's deferred-quarantine commits that wait for drain-fence ACK-EMITTED?
stressors.attractor: (a) Effective-capacity denominator drifts behind the latest commit because the calculator reads stale per-shard summaries that were not refreshed under the flap rate, and per-replica fan-out goes to evicted/draining replicas. (b) admit_evict_engine's floor check uses a stale denominator and admits a tip-class request to a replica already silently drained in a more recent flap. (c) deferred-quarantine entries pile up while drain-fence pre-emption holds the lane, and quarantine_eviction_engine surfaces no alert because its deferral counter is reset by the flap-induced commit churn.
stressors.solution: v0 has replica_health_register entries refreshed by commit_sequencer per transition but does not specify a per-shard summary watermark or coherence guarantee under high commit churn. Solution: (1) replica_health_register's per-(chain, fork_id) shard summary is computed inside commit_sequencer's CAS critical section and stamped with the shard's commit_hlc_watermark on every commit; readers (effective_capacity_calculator, admit_evict_engine, dispatch_validator) consume the summary through a read-your-writes path keyed by the watermark. (2) admit_evict_engine's safe-membership-floor read takes the same shard CAS lock as the proposed commit so the floor check cannot use a denominator from a watermark older than the proposal's submission_hlc. (3) quarantine_eviction_engine's deferred-quarantine alert counter is keyed by (chain, fork_id, replica_id) deferral_started_hlc — not by deferral count — so flap-induced commit churn does not reset the counter and an alert fires when ANY deferral has been pending longer than the documented threshold.

stressors.description: fork_detection_alerter (parent scope) signals a sub-pool repartition for (chain, prior_fork_id, new_fork_id). sub_pool_composition_engine must commit the new sub-pool's membership through commit_sequencer BEFORE chain_router's routing-table fence admits the new fork AND BEFORE chain_router emits the fork-transition handshake to fanout. Mid-reshape, fanout is briefly unreachable, the chain_router parent enters fork-transition-pending degraded mode, AND a drain-fence broadcast for tenant T arrives whose audit writes span both prior_fork_id and new_fork_id sub-pool views. Question: does sub_pool_composition_engine atomically commit the new membership without leaking partial sub-pool state visible to dispatch_validator (which would forward-progress on the new fork before the handshake-ack), AND does the drain-fence flush enumerate audit writes correctly across both sub-pool views while the new sub-pool's commit is mid-flight?
stressors.attractor: (a) dispatch_validator dispatches a forward-progress request on new_fork_id while the new sub-pool's membership commit is observed by replica_health_register but the fanout-handshake-ack has not been recorded — leaks fork-transition-pending semantics. (b) drain_fence_consumer's flush enumeration uses the post-transition replica_health_register summary alone, missing audit writes still in flight against the prior sub-pool view. (c) sub_pool_composition_engine commits a partial new-sub-pool membership (some replicas admitted, others still pending) and admit_evict_engine reads the partial state for floor calculations.
stressors.solution: v0 says sub_pool_composition_engine commits new sub-pool membership before the routing-table fence and dispatch_validator refuses forward-progress until handshake-ack is recorded, but it does not specify atomicity of the sub-pool reshape commit nor the dual-view enumeration during drain-fence flush. Solution: (1) sub_pool_composition_engine's reshape is a single multi-row CAS commit through commit_sequencer that atomically transitions ALL prior_fork_id memberships to new_fork_id sub-pool memberships under one shard CAS line per (chain, fork_id_pair); commit_sequencer rejects partial reshape commits and the engine retries from scratch on conflict. (2) dispatch_validator reads the per-(chain, fork_id) shard's fork_transition_state field (one of: stable, reshape-committed-handshake-pending, handshake-acked); refuses forward-progress on new_fork_id when state is reshape-committed-handshake-pending. (3) drain_fence_consumer, when admit_evict_engine flushes audit writes for tenant T, enumerates over the union of prior_fork_id and new_fork_id sub-pool views by reading both shard summaries through commit_sequencer and continuing enumeration across reshape commits using the commit_hlc_watermark.

stressors.description: A misconfigured tenant or a bug in upstream cost-class hint propagation drives a high-rate storm of dispatch attempts where requests arrive at dispatch_validator without a cost-class hint when one is required (long-RPC archive paths). Each refusal surfaces an alert. Concurrently, drain-fence broadcasts for that tenant land and drain-fence-priority lane is reserving CAS capacity on the per-(chain, fork_id) shard. Question: do refusal-storm alerts overwhelm phase_marker_journal write throughput on the same shard, AND does the drain-fence-priority lane's reservation block dispatch_validator's read-your-writes path keyed by commit_hlc_watermark causing dispatches to either stall or proceed against a stale watermark?
stressors.attractor: (a) phase_marker_journal write throughput is consumed by alert metadata for cost-class refusals, starving drain-fence flush phase-marker writes, causing drain-fence ack-window HLC budget to expire and rejecting legitimate broadcasts. (b) dispatch_validator's read-your-writes summary read blocks behind drain-fence-priority commit on the shard, and the validator falls back silently to a stale watermark, briefly admitting cost-class-less dispatches. (c) the alert counter for cost-class-less retries is global rather than per-(chain, fork_id, tenant_id), so the storm masks the real anomaly.
stressors.solution: v0 specifies dispatch_validator surfaces an alert on cost-class-less retry but does not isolate the alert path from the commit_sequencer CAS line, nor scope the alert counter, nor protect the read-your-writes summary from drain-fence-priority blocking. Solution: (1) dispatch_validator's refusal alert path is OUT-OF-BAND with respect to commit_sequencer: refusals do NOT write to phase_marker_journal under the shard CAS line — they write to a refusal_alert_buffer that is drained asynchronously and never blocks commits or summary reads. (2) dispatch_validator's read-your-writes summary read is shard-CAS-lock-FREE on the read path: it consumes a published per-shard summary snapshot whose commit_hlc_watermark advances monotonically; readers cannot block CAS commits and cannot dispatch against a watermark older than a documented bound (if older, the dispatch is bounced as retryable rather than served against stale state). (3) the cost-class-less retry alert counter is keyed by (chain, fork_id, tenant_id, hlc_window) so a misconfigured tenant's storm cannot mask another tenant's anomaly; documented per-tenant rate-limit on counter-driven alert emission.

stressors.description: lifecycle_gate (parent's parent) drives a bulk-eviction wave: dozens-to-hundreds of replicas across (chain, fork_id) sub-pools must be drained-then-evicted in a single window. Each eviction goes through admit_evict_engine + commit_sequencer + the safe-membership-floor check; quarantine_eviction_engine is also active; sub_pool_composition_engine is rebalancing in parallel because traffic share for some sub-pools is exceeding target due to mass-eviction. parent lifecycle_gate's bulk_admitter is also feeding admission proposals coupled to a shared budget. Question: under bulk-wave throughput, does commit_sequencer's serialization on each shard CAS line create per-shard backpressure that interacts with the safe-membership-floor read (now shard-locked per s2)? Does the floor check converge or oscillate? Does effective_capacity_calculator's denominator stay coherent when bulk admits and bulk evicts race on the same shard? Does the rate-limit on overrides per window get exceeded by bulk-wave admits, exhausting emergency capacity?
stressors.attractor: (a) per-shard CAS line saturates and bulk-wave evictions queue while admits proceed on a different shard, leaving an inconsistent global pool view across the wave window. (b) sub_pool_composition_engine's rebalance proposals contend for the same shard CAS line as evictions and the engine retries indefinitely, surfacing rebalance-stuck. (c) override_admission_engine's max-overrides-per-window counter trips during the wave because bulk_admitter (parent) is treating overrides as the fast-path and exhausts the emergency reserve, leaving no override headroom for genuine emergencies. (d) effective_capacity_calculator's denominator briefly inverts (more evicted than admitted in a window) during the wave and admit_evict_engine's floor check refuses an admit that would have been safe under the post-wave state.
stressors.solution: v0 has per-shard CAS serialization but no admission-class separation between bulk admits, override admits, and rebalance admits, so bulk-wave traffic exhausts the override rate-limit and starves rebalance proposals. Solution: (1) commit_sequencer's per-shard CAS line carries an admission-class lane discriminator: bulk-wave admits, override admits, rebalance admits, and quarantine evictions are routed to separate ordered queues on the same shard; the drain-fence-priority lane already pre-empts the rest; bulk-wave admits cannot starve rebalance admits because the engine round-robins across non-priority lanes within a documented per-shard fairness budget. (2) override_admission_engine's max-overrides-per-window counter distinguishes operator-emergency overrides from bulk_admitter-driven admits — bulk-wave admits do NOT consume the emergency override counter; they consume a separate bulk_admit counter that lifecycle_gate (parent's parent) sets via a parent-scope budget contract. (3) admit_evict_engine's floor check on bulk-wave admits is computed against the projected post-wave state for that wave_id (admitted in the wave so far minus evicted in the wave so far) so transient inversions during the wave do not refuse admits that converge to safe state by wave-completion. The wave_id is provided by lifecycle_gate (parent's parent) — the contract that an admission proposal carries a wave_id is a parent-scope concern bubbled up.
